answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a orchard as the anchor of the cost.
